correctness.rationale: For every prime power q>=2 and nontrivial additive character, group enumeration gives |SL_2(F_q)|=q(q^2-1). The exact one-coordinate, same-row/column and opposite-entry Fourier sums produce a Hermitian Gram with four coordinate blocks. Direct character orthogonality yields K_epsilon K_epsilon^*=q^2 I-(q+1)J, so its restriction to the mean-zero subspace has singular value q. The four mean-coordinate vectors decompose into a one-dimensional top bulk mode, two-dimensional bottom bulk mode, and a residual 2x2 block coupled to the constant character. The block characteristic polynomial gives both simple roots and a strictly positive determinant q(q-1)/(q+1)^2. Explicit discriminant comparisons prove the strict eigenvalue order for q>=2, and the exhibited eigenvectors classify all equality spaces. The standalone checker enumerated 3,090 matrices across q=2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11, verified both Kloosterman matrix identities, every Gram entry, eigenvalue with multiplicity and constructed eigenvectors (maximum numerical eigen error 2e-15). The general theorem is established by the exact proof rather than those finite tests.

originality.rationale: Searches of published research records, the available preceding ledgers, and relevant primary literature found no theorem covering the selected 4q-3 coordinate-wise additive character family on determinant-one matrices over every prime-power field. The closest direct source (Li--Hu 2011) gives ambient scalar Fourier transforms, but not their selected Gram eigenspectrum, sharp frame bounds, or complete eigenspaces; Thill--Hassibi uses nonabelian group-representation Fourier frames. The exact Kloosterman isometry and 5-dimensional coupled-block diagonalization provide new scientific content at the statement level beyond parameter substitution. The 2014 conference predecessor was not available in full, and equivalent older Kloosterman-matrix or frame-spectrum formulations remain priority risks.

value.rationale: The affine determinant-one quadric SL_2(F_q) is a canonical finite matrix variety, and the constant plus four one-coordinate Fourier bands are the natural lowest-complexity ambient additive measurements. Their condition number and redundancy are not determined by bounds on individual Kloosterman sums. The theorem provides a uniform four-level spectral classification for all prime powers, exact sharp frame bounds, a full high-dimensional equality space and an explicit lower extremizer. It proves quantitative near-orthogonality with squared Riesz ratio 1+4/q+O(q^-2), including characteristic two and all extension fields. This is a structural classification and natural sharp invariant, rather than a single arbitrary finite example or minor numerical improvement.
